Lakers Nation > Blog > Video > Lakers Video: Yaxel Lendeborg Looking Forward To Rematch With Luka Doncic Video Lakers Video: Yaxel Lendeborg Looking Forward To Rematch With Luka Doncic
 Ron Gutterman Published: 10/29/2026 3 Min Read Oct 21, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) drives to the basket against Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) in the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images SHARE The Los Angeles Lakers are 4-1 to begin the 2026-27 NBA season, starting that off with a dominant win over the Golden State Warriors on Opening Night. The story from that game was less the Lakers win, and more about the on-court battle between superstar Luka Doncic and 24-year-old rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. 
 Doncic had a game-high 28 points to go along with eight rebounds and seven assists. He was a game-high plus-31. Lendeborg made his NBA debut with 12 points and was a minus-21 on the night, but made headlines for going toe to toe with Doncic and trash talking him throughout the night, and especially in his postgame comments . Many circled their next meeting — less than two weeks later on Friday, Oct. 30 — as appointment viewing, and Lendeborg recently added fuel to that fire, via Anthony Slater of ESPN : 
 Is Yaxel Lendeborg looking forward to the Lakers game on Friday?
 “Absolutely. Absolutely. Yes, I am. I’ll talk about that on Friday.” https://t.co/31b3isk3dI
 — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 29, 2026 
 Lendeborg’s confidence has been one of the defining features of his rookie season thus far, both in the offseason and now. He’s been able to back it up, though. He had scored 26 or more points in each of his last three games, leading the Warriors to wins in two of them. He’s averaging 22.6 points and 9.2 rebounds per game through five contests in his rookie season.
 And he will likely spend much of Friday’s game matched up with Doncic, who’s leading the NBA with 36.0 points per game. Doncic has certainly seen this video of Lendeborg and is going to give him everything he can handle on Friday. If Lendeborg can keep his composure, it should make for a very fun game. If not, L.A. may have their way with the Warriors similarly to Opening Night. 
 JJ Redick: Luka Doncic becomes showman when in flow state
 Friday represents the perfect opportunity for Doncic to play his best type of game. He has external motivation to dominate, is coming off of two days rest after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the L.A. Clippers and is already off to a hot start to begin the season. 
 Lakers head coach JJ Redick called Doncic a showman when he is in that type of state. 
 “I think for him in particular, when he’s in the flow state he gets into showman mode,” Redick said after the game on Spectrum SportsNet. “He’s on a stage performing and that’s always really fun to watch.”
